departments.name: Foreign investment and foreign trade (RBI, DGFT)
departments.desc: Reports to the Reserve Bank on foreign investment, overseas investment and foreign loans, export proceeds, and the yearly update of the Importer-Exporter Code.

departments.name: Labour and workplace
departments.desc: Wage payment dates, the yearly workplace-harassment report, and State shop and establishment registration and returns.

departments.name: Licences, registrations and data
departments.desc: Food licence, packaged goods registration, trade mark renewal, cyber incident and personal data duties, and other sector-neutral registrations.

questions.text: Does a person or company resident outside India hold shares in the business, or a capital contribution in the LLP?
questions.help: Foreign direct investment that is still outstanding on 31 March. Share application money alone, and shares issued on a non-repatriable basis, do not count.

questions.text: Have you invested in a company or business outside India (overseas direct investment)?
questions.help: For example a foreign subsidiary or joint venture, or 10% or more of the equity of a foreign entity. Listed foreign shares bought as a portfolio investment are not meant here.

questions.text: Did it issue shares or other equity instruments to a person resident outside India, or (for an LLP) receive a capital contribution from one?
questions.help: Each allotment to a foreign investor is reported to the Reserve Bank through the company's bank.

questions.text: Did you buy shares of an Indian company from a person resident outside India, or sell them to one?
questions.help: A transfer of equity instruments between a resident and a non-resident. The resident buyer or seller reports it.

questions.text: Was a capital contribution or profit share in the LLP transferred between a resident and a non-resident?
questions.help: In either direction: a non-resident partner coming in by buying a resident partner's share, or leaving by selling it.

questions.text: Is it foreign owned or controlled, and did it invest in another Indian company or LLP?
questions.help: A downstream investment by an Indian entity that itself has foreign investment counts as indirect foreign investment in the entity it invests in.

questions.text: Did the company issue employee stock options to employees or directors who are resident outside India?
questions.help: Including employees or directors of its holding company, joint venture or overseas subsidiaries.

questions.text: Has it borrowed from a lender outside India (an external commercial borrowing)?
questions.help: A loan, bond or other debt raised from a recognised non-resident lender, such as a foreign parent or a foreign bank.

questions.text: Do you export goods or services?
questions.help: Selling goods or services to customers outside India, whether or not you are registered for GST.

questions.text: Do you hold an Importer-Exporter Code (IEC)?
questions.help: The 10-character code from the Directorate General of Foreign Trade that is needed to import or export.

questions.text: Was the company incorporated within the last 12 months?
questions.help: New companies with a share capital must file a declaration before they start business or borrow.

questions.text: Did the company give security for a loan this year (create or change a charge on its assets)?
questions.help: For example a mortgage, hypothecation or pledge in favour of a bank or other lender.

questions.text: Did the company pass a special resolution, or another resolution or agreement that must be filed with the Registrar?
questions.help: For example a change to the articles, a change of name or objects, or a board resolution of a kind the Act lists.

questions.text: Was a director or key managerial person appointed, or did one resign or change, this year?
questions.help: Each appointment and each change is notified to the Registrar.

questions.text: Does the company have a net worth of Rs 500 crore or more, a turnover of Rs 1,000 crore or more, or a net profit of Rs 5 crore or more?
questions.help: Above any one of these the corporate social responsibility (CSR) provisions apply.

questions.text: Is it a food business with an FSSAI licence or registration?
questions.help: Making, packing, storing, transporting, selling, serving or importing food. Small operators with turnover up to Rs 12 lakh hold a registration; larger ones hold a licence.

questions.text: Does it manufacture, repack or relabel food, or import food, under an FSSAI licence?
questions.help: Licensed manufacturers (including those who have products made for them by others), importers and manufacturer-exporters file a yearly return. Holders of a registration certificate do not.

questions.text: Do you pre-pack goods for sale, or import packaged goods?
questions.help: Putting any commodity into a package for sale, distribution or delivery, or importing such packages.

questions.text: Do you own a registered trade mark?
questions.help: A mark entered on the register of the Trade Marks Registry, not one that is only applied for.

questions.text: On what date does the current trade mark registration expire?
questions.help: It is ten years from the date of registration and is shown on the registration or renewal certificate. Leave it blank if you do not know.

questions.text: Do you collect or use personal data of individuals in digital form?
questions.help: Names, phone numbers, addresses, identity or payment details of customers, users or employees held on a computer, app or website.

questions.text: Do you put plastic packaging on the Indian market as a producer, importer or brand owner?
questions.help: Making or importing plastic packaging, importing products in plastic packaging, or selling goods under your brand in plastic packaging.

questions.text: Does the business hold a Udyam (MSME) registration?
questions.help: The free registration of micro, small and medium enterprises on the Ministry of MSME's portal.

questions.text: Is it registered, or does it have prior permission, to receive foreign contributions under the FCRA?
questions.help: Charities and associations that receive donations from foreign sources need registration or prior permission from the Ministry of Home Affairs.

compliances.name: Annual return on foreign liabilities and assets
compliances.form: FLA Return (on the RBI's FLAIR portal)
compliances.head: Foreign investment reporting
compliances.brief: A yearly return to the Reserve Bank by every Indian entity that has foreign direct investment in it, or has invested in a business abroad. It can be filed on unaudited figures and revised later.
compliances.why: The business has foreign investment in it, or has an investment abroad, outstanding at the end of March.
compliances.appliesInWords: Indian-resident companies, LLPs, partnership and proprietary firms and other entities that have received FDI or made overseas direct investment, in the reporting year or the year before. Not needed when only share application money was received, or when shares were issued on a non-repatriable basis.
compliances.dueText: By 15 July of the reporting year, on audited or unaudited financials.
compliances.penalty: Non-filing of the return before the due date is treated as a violation of FEMA and the penalty clause may be invoked. Late Submission Fee of Rs 7,500. Non-filing is treated as a violation of FEMA.
compliances.evidence: are mandatorily required to submit/file FLA return under FEMA 1999 by July 15 of reporting year
compliances.note: A return filed after 15 July needs the Reserve Bank's approval first.

compliances.name: Report shares issued to a foreign investor
compliances.head: Foreign investment reporting
compliances.brief: An Indian company that issues shares or other equity instruments to a person resident outside India reports each issue to the Reserve Bank through its bank.
compliances.why: The company issued equity instruments to a person resident outside India.
compliances.appliesInWords: An Indian company issuing equity instruments to a person resident outside India, where the issue counts as foreign direct investment.

due.text: Not later than thirty days from the date of issue of the equity instruments

compliances.dueText: Not later than thirty days from the date of issue of equity instruments.
compliances.penalty: Late Submission Fee of Rs 7,500 plus 0.025% of the amount involved for each year of delay, capped at 100% of the amount. The option to pay it is open for three years from the due date.
compliances.evidence: not later than thirty days from the date of issue of equity instruments

compliances.name: Report a foreign capital contribution to an LLP
compliances.head: Foreign investment reporting
compliances.brief: An LLP that receives money from a person resident outside India for a capital contribution and share of profits reports it to the Reserve Bank.
compliances.why: The LLP received a capital contribution from a person resident outside India.
compliances.appliesInWords: An LLP receiving consideration for capital contribution and acquisition of profit shares from a person resident outside India.

due.text: Within 30 days from the date of receipt of the amount of consideration

compliances.dueText: Within 30 days from the date of receipt of the amount of consideration.
compliances.penalty: Late Submission Fee of Rs 7,500 plus 0.025% of the amount involved for each year of delay, capped at 100% of the amount. The option to pay it is open for three years from the due date.
compliances.evidence: within 30 days from the date of receipt of the amount of consideration

compliances.name: Report a share transfer between a resident and a non-resident
compliances.head: Foreign investment reporting
compliances.brief: When shares of an Indian company pass between a resident and a person resident outside India, the resident buyer or seller reports the transfer to the Reserve Bank through a bank.
compliances.why: You bought shares of an Indian company from a non-resident, or sold them to one.
compliances.appliesInWords: The resident transferor or transferee (or the non-resident holding on a non-repatriable basis) in a transfer of equity instruments of an Indian company.

due.text: Within sixty days of the transfer of the equity instruments or of the receipt or remittance of funds, whichever is earlier

compliances.dueText: Within sixty days of transfer of equity instruments or receipt / remittance of funds, whichever is earlier.
compliances.penalty: Late Submission Fee of Rs 7,500 plus 0.025% of the amount involved for each year of delay, capped at 100% of the amount. The option to pay it is open for three years from the due date.
compliances.evidence: within sixty days of transfer of equity instruments or receipt / remittance of funds whichever is earlier

compliances.name: Report a transfer of an LLP share between a resident and a non-resident
compliances.head: Foreign investment reporting
compliances.brief: A disinvestment or transfer of capital contribution or profit share in an LLP between a resident and a non-resident, in either direction, is reported by the resident party.
compliances.why: A capital contribution or profit share in the LLP moved between a resident and a non-resident.
compliances.appliesInWords: The resident transferor or transferee of a capital contribution or profit share in an LLP.

due.text: Within 60 days from the date of receipt of funds

compliances.dueText: Within 60 days from the date of receipt of funds.
compliances.penalty: Late Submission Fee of Rs 7,500 plus 0.025% of the amount involved for each year of delay, capped at 100% of the amount. The option to pay it is open for three years from the due date.
compliances.evidence: within 60 days from the date of receipt of funds

compliances.name: Report a downstream investment
compliances.head: Foreign investment reporting
compliances.brief: An Indian entity that itself has foreign investment and invests in another Indian entity reports that downstream investment, which counts as indirect foreign investment.
compliances.why: It is foreign owned or controlled and invested in another Indian entity.
compliances.appliesInWords: An Indian entity or investment vehicle making a downstream investment in another Indian entity that is treated as indirect foreign investment.

due.text: Within 30 days from the date of allotment of the equity instruments

compliances.dueText: Within 30 days from the date of allotment of equity instruments.
compliances.penalty: Late Submission Fee of Rs 7,500 plus 0.025% of the amount involved for each year of delay, capped at 100% of the amount. The option to pay it is open for three years from the due date.
compliances.evidence: within 30 days from the date of allotment of equity instruments

compliances.name: Report stock options issued to non-resident employees
compliances.head: Foreign investment reporting
compliances.brief: An Indian company that issues employee stock options to employees or directors resident outside India reports the issue to the Reserve Bank.
compliances.why: The company issued stock options to employees or directors resident outside India.
compliances.appliesInWords: An Indian company issuing employees' stock options to persons resident outside India who are its employees or directors, or those of its holding company, joint venture or overseas subsidiaries.

due.text: Within 30 days from the date of issue of the employees' stock option

compliances.dueText: Within 30 days from the date of issue of employees' stock option.
compliances.penalty: Late Submission Fee of Rs 7,500 plus 0.025% of the amount involved for each year of delay, capped at 100% of the amount. The option to pay it is open for three years from the due date.
compliances.evidence: within 30 days from the date of issue of employees' stock option

compliances.name: Get a loan registration number before drawing a foreign loan
compliances.head: Foreign borrowing
compliances.brief: Before any money is drawn under an external commercial borrowing, the borrower reports the loan terms through its bank and obtains a Loan Registration Number (LRN) from the Reserve Bank. Later changes to the terms are reported on a revised form.
compliances.why: It has borrowed, or is about to borrow, from a lender outside India.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every borrower raising an external commercial borrowing.

due.text: Before the first draw-down of the loan; changes in terms not later than 7 days after they take effect

compliances.dueText: Any draw-down should happen only after obtaining the LRN from the Reserve Bank. Changes in the loan terms: a revised Form ECB not later than 7 days from the changes effected.
compliances.penalty: Late Submission Fee of Rs 7,500 plus 0.025% of the amount involved for each year of delay, capped at 100% of the amount. The option to pay it is open for three years from the due date.
compliances.evidence: Any draw-down in respect of an ECB should happen only after obtaining the LRN from the Reserve Bank.

compliances.name: Monthly return on a foreign loan
compliances.head: Foreign borrowing
compliances.brief: A borrower with an external commercial borrowing reports the actual transactions under the loan every month, through its bank, to the Reserve Bank's statistics department.
compliances.why: It has an external commercial borrowing outstanding.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every borrower with an external commercial borrowing, for each month until the loan is fully repaid.

due.text: Within seven working days from the close of each month

compliances.dueText: So as to reach the Reserve Bank within seven working days from the close of the month to which it relates.
compliances.penalty: Late Submission Fee of Rs 7,500 plus 0.025% of the amount involved for each year of delay, capped at 100% of the amount. The option to pay it is open for three years from the due date.
compliances.evidence: within seven working days from the close of month to which it relates
compliances.note: A borrower that has not filed its returns for eight quarters or more can be treated as untraceable, and its bank will not process a fresh borrowing.

compliances.name: Report an overseas investment when it is made
compliances.head: Overseas investment
compliances.brief: A resident who makes an overseas direct investment, or any other financial commitment to a foreign entity, reports it through a bank and obtains a Unique Identification Number.
compliances.why: You have invested, or are about to invest, in a business outside India.
compliances.appliesInWords: A person resident in India making a financial commitment (equity, loan or guarantee) to a foreign entity.

due.text: At the time of sending the outward remittance or making the financial commitment, whichever is earlier

compliances.dueText: At the time of sending outward remittance or making a financial commitment, whichever is earlier. Form FC goes to the bank on or before making the initial investment.
compliances.penalty: A delayed report may be filed with a Late Submission Fee for up to three years from the due date. Until the delay is regularised, no further financial commitment may be made to that foreign entity.
compliances.evidence: at the time of sending outward remittance or making a financial commitment, whichever is earlier

compliances.name: Annual performance report on an overseas investment
compliances.head: Overseas investment
compliances.brief: A resident who holds an overseas direct investment files a yearly report on each foreign entity, based on its accounts. Where a statutory audit does not apply, a chartered accountant certifies it.
compliances.why: You hold an investment in a business outside India.
compliances.appliesInWords: A person resident in India who has acquired equity capital in a foreign entity that counts as overseas direct investment. Not required when the holding is less than 10% of the equity without control and there is no other financial commitment, or when the foreign entity is under liquidation.
compliances.dueText: Every year by 31 December. Where the foreign entity's accounting year ends on 31 December, by 31 December of the next year.
compliances.penalty: Late Submission Fee of Rs 7,500. Non-filing is treated as a violation of FEMA. Until the delay is regularised, no further financial commitment may be made to that foreign entity.
compliances.evidence: by 31st December

compliances.name: Bring export proceeds back to India in time
compliances.form: Export Declaration Form (EDF), with the shipping bill
compliances.head: Exports
compliances.brief: An exporter declares each export of goods in the Export Declaration Form and must realise the full export value and bring it to India within the period the Reserve Bank sets. A bank can extend the period on request.
compliances.why: You export goods or services.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every exporter of goods or services from India.

due.text: Within nine months from the date of shipment (goods) or of invoice (services); twelve months when invoiced or settled in Indian Rupees

compliances.dueText: Nine months from the date of shipment in case of goods and from the date of invoice in case of services; twelve months where the export is invoiced or settled in Indian Rupees.
compliances.penalty: If proceeds remain unrealised beyond one year from the due date, further exports may be made only against full advance payment or an irrevocable letter of credit.
compliances.evidence: nine months from the date of shipment in case of goods
compliances.note: These regulations took effect on 1 October 2026. The periods were fifteen and eighteen months until a September 2026 amendment cut them to nine and twelve; check the current text before relying on them.

compliances.name: Update the Importer-Exporter Code every year
compliances.form: IEC updation on the DGFT portal
compliances.head: Imports and exports
compliances.brief: Every holder of an Importer-Exporter Code confirms or updates its details online once a year, even when nothing has changed.
compliances.why: You hold an Importer-Exporter Code.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every IEC holder.
compliances.dueText: Every year, during the April to June period.
compliances.penalty: An IEC that is not updated within the period is de-activated. It is activated again once it is updated.
compliances.evidence: An IEC holder has to ensure that details in its IEC is updated electronically every year, during the April-June period.

compliances.name: Declaration before a new company starts business
compliances.head: Company filings
compliances.brief: A new company with a share capital cannot start business or borrow until a director files a declaration that every subscriber has paid for the shares they agreed to take, and the registered office has been verified.
compliances.why: The company was incorporated in the last 12 months.
compliances.appliesInWords: A company with a share capital incorporated after the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2019 came into force.

due.text: Within 180 days of the date of incorporation

compliances.dueText: Within a period of one hundred and eighty days of the date of incorporation of the company.
compliances.penalty: Penalty of Rs 50,000 on the company, and Rs 1,000 a day (up to Rs 1,00,000) on each officer in default. The Registrar may also start removing the company's name from the register.
compliances.evidence: a declaration is filed by a director within a period of one hundred and eighty days of the date of incorporation of the company
compliances.note: The form number INC-20A is the name given in your brief; it was not read on an official page. The time limit and penalty were read in the 2019 amending Act as passed; later changes to the penalty were not checked.

compliances.name: Register a charge on the company's assets
compliances.head: Company filings
compliances.brief: When a company gives security over its property or assets, it registers the particulars of the charge with the Registrar of Companies.
compliances.why: The company created or changed a charge on its assets this year.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every company creating a charge on its property, assets or undertakings, in or outside India.

due.text: Within thirty days of the creation of the charge

compliances.dueText: Within thirty days of its creation. On application the Registrar may allow registration within sixty days of creation on payment of additional fees, and within a further sixty days on payment of ad valorem fees.
compliances.evidence: with the Registrar within thirty days of its creation
compliances.note: The thirty days were read in the Act as passed in 2013 and the extended periods in the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2019. The form number CHG-1 was not read on an official page.

compliances.name: Hold board meetings
compliances.head: Company meetings
compliances.brief: The board of directors meets at least four times a year. A One Person Company, a small company and a dormant company need only one meeting in each half of the calendar year.
compliances.why: It is a company.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every company. A One Person Company with only one director is outside this rule.

due.text: At least four meetings a year, with not more than 120 days between two meetings

compliances.dueText: First meeting within thirty days of incorporation; then at least four meetings every year with not more than one hundred and twenty days between two consecutive meetings. One Person, small and dormant companies: at least one meeting in each half of a calendar year, with a gap of not less than ninety days.
compliances.evidence: hold a minimum number of four meetings of its Board of Directors every year in such a manner that not more than one hundred and twenty days shall intervene between two consecutive meetings
compliances.note: Read only in the Act as passed in 2013 (Gazette copy on nclt.gov.in). mca.gov.in and indiacode.nic.in refused access, so it could not be confirmed that this section has not been amended or relaxed by notification since.

compliances.name: File resolutions and agreements with the Registrar
compliances.head: Company filings
compliances.brief: A copy of every special resolution, and of the other resolutions and agreements the Act lists, is filed with the Registrar of Companies.
compliances.why: The company passed a resolution or made an agreement that must be filed.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every company that passes a resolution or makes an agreement of a kind listed in section 117(3).

due.text: Within thirty days of passing the resolution or making the agreement

compliances.dueText: Within thirty days of the passing or making thereof.
compliances.penalty: As substituted in 2019: Rs 1,00,000 on the company plus Rs 500 a day (up to Rs 25,00,000), and Rs 50,000 on each officer in default plus Rs 500 a day (up to Rs 5,00,000).
compliances.evidence: shall be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of the passing or making thereof
compliances.note: The thirty days were read only in the Act as passed in 2013; later amendments, the exemptions for private companies and the form number MGT-14 were not read on an official page. The penalty is the 2019 text and may have been reduced since.

compliances.name: Notify a change of directors or key managerial personnel
compliances.head: Company filings
compliances.brief: A return of the particulars of directors and key managerial personnel is filed with the Registrar on every appointment and every change.
compliances.why: A director or key managerial person was appointed or changed this year.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every company, on the appointment of a director or key managerial person and on any change.

due.text: Within thirty days of the appointment or change

compliances.dueText: Within thirty days from the appointment of every director and key managerial personnel, and within thirty days of any change taking place.
compliances.evidence: shall be filed with the Registrar within thirty days from the appointment of every director and key managerial personnel
compliances.note: Read only in the Act as passed in 2013; later amendments and the form number DIR-12 were not read on an official page.

compliances.name: Transfer unspent CSR money
compliances.form: Unspent Corporate Social Responsibility Account; Schedule VII fund
compliances.head: Corporate social responsibility
compliances.brief: A company covered by the corporate social responsibility rules that has not spent the required amount moves it: money for an ongoing project goes to a special bank account, and any other unspent money goes to a government fund listed in Schedule VII.
compliances.why: The company is above the CSR thresholds.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every company with a net worth of Rs 500 crore or more, a turnover of Rs 1,000 crore or more, or a net profit of Rs 5 crore or more, that has an unspent CSR amount for the year.
compliances.dueText: Ongoing projects: transfer to the Unspent Corporate Social Responsibility Account within thirty days from the end of the financial year. Other unspent amounts: transfer to a Schedule VII fund within six months of the expiry of the financial year.
compliances.penalty: As passed in 2019: a fine of Rs 50,000 to Rs 25,00,000 on the company, with a fine or imprisonment for officers in default.
compliances.evidence: shall be transferred by the company within a period of thirty days from the end of the financial year to a special account
compliances.note: Read in the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2019 as passed. Whether and when this section was brought into force, later changes to the penalty, and the annual CSR report form (CSR-2) could not be read on an official page. The thresholds were read in the Act as passed in 2013.

compliances.name: Annual report on workplace sexual harassment complaints
compliances.form: Annual report of the Internal Committee
compliances.head: Workplace
compliances.authority: District Officer (District Magistrate) under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act
compliances.brief: Every workplace with ten or more workers has an Internal Committee. Each calendar year the committee reports the number of complaints received and disposed of to the employer and the District Officer, and the employer states the numbers in its own annual report.
compliances.why: You have ten or more employees.
compliances.appliesInWords: The Internal Committee of every employer with ten or more workers, and the employer.
compliances.dueText: A report for each calendar year. The New Delhi district office asks for the report for 1 January to 31 December to be filed latest by 31 January of the next year; other districts set their own date.
compliances.penalty: Fine up to Rs 50,000 for an employer who fails to constitute the committee or to report; double on a repeat conviction.
compliances.evidence: shall in each calendar year prepare, in such form and at such time as may be prescribed, an annual report and submit the same to the employer and the District Officer
compliances.note: The Act fixes the calendar year but not the date. 31 January was read on the New Delhi District Magistrate's notice (last updated 16 January 2024) and applies to that district; confirm the date with your own District Officer. The 31 January date was read on a district administration notice, not in the Act or its Rules: confirm it for your district.

compliances.name: Pay wages on time
compliances.form: Wage payment under the Code on Wages, 2019
compliances.head: Wages
compliances.authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment and State labour departments
compliances.brief: The Code on Wages, one of the four labour codes the Government has implemented, sets time limits for paying wages to every employee, whatever their salary.
compliances.why: You pay salaries.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every employer, for all employees.
compliances.dueText: Monthly-rated employees: within 7 days of the next month. Daily wages at the end of the shift, weekly wages before the weekly holiday, fortnightly wages within 2 days of the end of the fortnight, and on termination or resignation within 2 working days.
compliances.evidence: Monthly-rated employee Within 7 days of the next month
compliances.note: Read on the Press Information Bureau's official explainer of 5 December 2025, not in the Code or its rules (labour.gov.in refused access).

compliances.name: Single annual return under the labour codes
compliances.form: Unified annual return (Shram Suvidha Portal or the State labour portal)
compliances.head: Labour returns
compliances.authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment and State labour departments
compliances.brief: The four labour codes replace the separate returns under 29 earlier labour laws with one electronic return. The form and date are set by the Central rules and by each State's rules.
compliances.why: You have employees.
compliances.appliesInWords: Employers and establishments covered by the labour codes.

due.text: Set by the Central or State rules under the labour codes: confirm on the Shram Suvidha Portal or your State labour portal

compliances.dueText: Not read on an official page. The government's explainer says only that there is a single return.
compliances.evidence: concept of a Single Registration, Single License, and Single Return
compliances.note: The four codes are reported to have taken effect on 21 November 2025 and Central rules to have been notified in May 2026 (both seen only in search results; pib.gov.in returned 403). labour.gov.in, shramsuvidha.gov.in and egazette.gov.in refused access, so the return's form, due date and penalty could not be read. Returns under the old Acts (maternity benefit, contract labour, factories, bonus, gratuity) should not be assumed to continue.

compliances.name: Maharashtra shops and establishments annual return
compliances.head: Shops and establishments
compliances.brief: Every employer of a shop or commercial establishment in Maharashtra uploads a yearly return for the calendar year.
compliances.why: You employ people in Maharashtra.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every employer of an establishment covered by the Maharashtra Shops and Establishments (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 2017.
compliances.dueText: Within two months for the year ending on 31 December.
compliances.evidence: shall online upload the Annual Return in Form ‘R’ on the website within two months for the year ending on 31st December
compliances.note: The rules were read as notified on 23 March 2018; later amendments were not checked.

compliances.name: Maharashtra: register the establishment and notify changes
compliances.form: Form A (ten or more workers), Form F (fewer than ten), Form I (changes)
compliances.head: Shops and establishments
compliances.brief: An establishment with ten or more workers applies online for registration; one with fewer than ten sends an online intimation that it has started business. Any change to the registered details is notified online.
compliances.why: You employ people in Maharashtra.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every employer of a shop or commercial establishment in Maharashtra.

due.text: Changes: within thirty days from the date the change took place

compliances.dueText: Changes in the certificate of registration: within thirty days from the date the change took place. The certificate is to be renewed thirty days before its expiry.
compliances.evidence: shall be notified online in Form ‘I’ to the Facilitator as per section 9 of the Act within thirty days from the date the change took place
compliances.note: The time limit for the first registration or intimation is in the Act, which could not be read. The rules were read as notified on 23 March 2018; later amendments were not checked.

compliances.name: Delhi shops and establishments registration
compliances.head: Shops and establishments
compliances.authority: Chief Inspector of Shops and Establishments, Delhi
compliances.brief: The occupier of every shop or commercial establishment in Delhi sends a statement to the Chief Inspector to register it.
compliances.why: You run an establishment in Delhi.
compliances.appliesInWords: The occupier of every establishment in Delhi.

due.text: Within ninety days of the date on which the establishment commences its work

compliances.dueText: New establishments: within ninety days from the date on which the establishment commences the work.
compliances.evidence: Within ninety days from the date mentioned in column 2 below ... The date on which the establishment commences the work.
compliances.note: Read in the Act as shown on the Delhi Labour Department's site, which gives no amendment date. The department's site says registration is now done online; companies newly incorporated in Delhi are reported to register through the incorporation form.

compliances.name: Delhi: notify changes to, or closure of, the establishment
compliances.head: Shops and establishments
compliances.authority: Chief Inspector of Shops and Establishments, Delhi
compliances.brief: The occupier tells the Chief Inspector when any registered detail changes and when the establishment closes.
compliances.why: You run an establishment in Delhi.
compliances.appliesInWords: The occupier of every registered establishment in Delhi.

due.text: Changes within thirty days; closure within fifteen days

compliances.dueText: Changes: within thirty days after the change has taken place. Closure: within fifteen days of closing the establishment.
compliances.evidence: within thirty days after the change has taken place

compliances.name: FSSAI annual return
compliances.head: Food business
compliances.authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
compliances.brief: Licensed food manufacturers (including repackers and relabellers), importers and manufacturer-exporters report the food handled in the previous financial year.
compliances.why: It manufactures or imports food under an FSSAI licence.
compliances.appliesInWords: FSSAI-licensed manufacturers, repackers, relabellers, importers and manufacturer-exporters. Holders of a registration certificate are not required to file.
compliances.dueText: By 31 May every year, for the food business activities of the previous financial year.
compliances.penalty: Rs 100 per day from 1 June, up to a maximum of 5 times the annual licence fee. No request to waive it is considered.
compliances.evidence: Last Date without penalty: 31st May every year

compliances.name: Renew the FSSAI licence or registration
compliances.form: Renewal application on the FoSCoS portal
compliances.head: Food business
compliances.authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
compliances.brief: An FSSAI licence or registration is issued for one to five years and is renewed before it expires. The application can be made up to 180 days early.
compliances.why: It is a food business with an FSSAI licence or registration.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every food business operator holding an FSSAI licence or registration.

due.text: Not later than 30 days before the licence expires

compliances.dueText: Not later than 30 days prior to the expiry of the licence, to avoid the late fee.
compliances.penalty: Late fee of Rs 100 per day in the last 30 days before expiry. After expiry: three times the annual fee from the 1st to the 90th day, and five times from the 91st to the 180th day.
compliances.evidence: a renewal has to be filed not later than 30 days prior to the expiry of License to avoid the late fee
compliances.note: Read on FSSAI's FAQ last updated 21 December 2022; a newer edition could not be opened.

compliances.name: Register as a packer or importer of packaged goods
compliances.form: Registration under rule 27, Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011
compliances.head: Packaged goods
compliances.authority: Director of Legal Metrology (Centre) or the State Controller of Legal Metrology
compliances.brief: Anyone who pre-packs any commodity for sale, or imports packaged commodities, registers their name and complete address with the legal metrology authority.
compliances.why: You pre-pack goods for sale or import packaged goods.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every individual, firm, Hindu undivided family, society, company or corporation that pre-packs or imports any commodity for sale, distribution or delivery.

due.text: Within ninety days from the date you start pre-packing or importing

compliances.dueText: Within ninety days from the date on which pre-packing or importing commences.
compliances.evidence: within ninety days from the date on which he or it commences such pre-packing
compliances.note: Read in the Department's compilation of the rules 'with all amendments' dated May 2022; changes after that were not checked. The application fee stated there is Rs 500.

compliances.name: Renew a registered trade mark
compliances.head: Intellectual property
compliances.brief: A trade mark registration lasts ten years and can be renewed for ten years at a time.
compliances.why: You own a registered trade mark.
compliances.appliesInWords: The registered proprietor of a trade mark.
compliances.dueText: Before the registration expires, every ten years. A late renewal is accepted with a surcharge within six months from the expiration of the last registration.
compliances.penalty: A mark not renewed may be removed from the register. It can be restored after six months and within one year from the expiration of the last registration.
compliances.evidence: for a period of ten years from the date of expiration of the original registration
compliances.note: The form number TM-R comes from the Registry's forms list seen in search results, not from the Act.

compliances.name: Report a cyber security incident
compliances.head: Cyber security
compliances.brief: Listed kinds of cyber incident, such as a data breach, ransomware or unauthorised access, are reported to CERT-In. Logs of all ICT systems are kept in India for a rolling 180 days.
compliances.why: It is a company, LLP or firm that runs computer systems.
compliances.appliesInWords: Any service provider, intermediary, data centre, body corporate and Government organisation.

due.text: Within 6 hours of noticing the incident or being told about it

compliances.dueText: Within 6 hours of noticing such incidents or being brought to notice about such incidents.
compliances.penalty: Failure to furnish the information or to comply may invite punitive action under section 70B(7) of the Information Technology Act, 2000.
compliances.evidence: shall mandatorily report cyber incidents as mentioned in Annexure I to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing such incidents
compliances.note: The directions took effect 60 days after 28 April 2022. CERT-In's site lists a later extension of the enforcement date for MSMEs (27 June 2022), which was not read.

compliances.name: Personal data protection duties (phased in)
compliances.form: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and Rules, 2025
compliances.head: Data protection
compliances.authority: Data Protection Board of India; Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
compliances.brief: Any business that decides why and how personal data is processed must give a clear consent notice, tell affected people about a data breach, publish a contact for data queries and answer access, correction and erasure requests.
compliances.why: You collect or use personal data in digital form.
compliances.appliesInWords: Every Data Fiduciary: an entity that decides why and how digital personal data is processed.

due.text: Breach: inform affected individuals without delay. Requests: answer within ninety days

compliances.dueText: The Rules were notified on 14 November 2025 with an eighteen-month period for phased compliance. On a breach, inform all affected individuals without delay. Requests for access, correction, updating or erasure: within a maximum of ninety days.
compliances.penalty: Up to Rs 250 crore for failing to keep reasonable security safeguards; up to Rs 200 crore for not notifying the Board or affected individuals of a breach; up to Rs 50 crore for other violations.
compliances.evidence: The Rules introduce an eighteen-month period for phased compliance.
compliances.note: Read on the government's explainer, not in the Rules (meity.gov.in refused access). The exact date each duty starts, and the time limit for the detailed breach report to the Board, could not be read and must be confirmed.

confirmations.dueText: Within six months from the date of closing of the financial year (first meeting: within nine months from the close of the first financial year); not more than fifteen months between two meetings. One Person Companies are exempt. The Registrar may extend the time, other than for the first meeting, by up to three months.
confirmations.evidence: in case of the first annual general meeting, it shall be held within a period of nine months from the date of closing of the first financial year of the company and in any other case, within a period of six months, from the date of closing of the financial year
confirmations.caveat: Section 96(1), read in the Companies Act, 2013 as published in the Gazette on 30 August 2013 (copy hosted by the National Company Law Tribunal). Amendments after 2013 could not be read: mca.gov.in, indiacode.nic.in and incometaxindia.gov.in returned 403.

confirmations.dueText: Within thirty days of the date of the annual general meeting. If no meeting was held: within thirty days of the last date before which it should have been held.
confirmations.evidence: shall be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of the date of annual general meeting
confirmations.penalty: Section 137(3) as amended in 2019: the company is liable to a penalty of Rs 1,000 for every day of default (the 2013 text caps this at Rs 10 lakh), and the officers in default to Rs 1,00,000 plus Rs 100 a day, up to Rs 5,00,000. Later reductions were not checked.
confirmations.caveat: Section 137(1), read in the Act as passed in 2013; penalty wording from the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2019 (https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3e2ad76f2326fbc6b56a45a56c59fafdb/uploads/2018/05/2023010354.pdf). The form number AOC-4 and the reported fee waiver for FY 2025-26 (to 31 December 2026) were not read on an official page.

confirmations.dueText: Within one hundred eighty days from the closure of the financial year.
confirmations.evidence: a One Person Company shall file a copy of the financial statements duly adopted by its member, along with all the documents which are required to be attached to such financial statements, within one hundred eighty days from the closure of the financial year
confirmations.caveat: Third proviso to section 137(1), read in the Act as passed in 2013; later amendments not checked.

confirmations.dueText: Within sixty days from the date on which the annual general meeting is held; where no meeting is held, within sixty days from the date on which it should have been held.
confirmations.evidence: Every company shall file with the Registrar a copy of the annual return, within sixty days from the date on which the annual general meeting is held
confirmations.penalty: Section 92(5) as substituted in 2019: penalty of Rs 50,000 on the company and on every officer in default, plus Rs 100 for each day the failure continues, up to Rs 5,00,000. Later reductions were not checked.
confirmations.caveat: Section 92(4), read in the Act as passed in 2013; penalty from the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2019. The form numbers MGT-7 and MGT-7A and the reported fee waiver for FY 2025-26 (to 31 January 2027) were not read on an official page.

confirmations.dueText: The same section 92(4) time limit: within sixty days from the date of the annual general meeting, or from the date it should have been held.
confirmations.evidence: Every company shall file with the Registrar a copy of the annual return, within sixty days from the date on which the annual general meeting is held
confirmations.caveat: The abridged form MGT-7A for small companies and One Person Companies was not read on an official page; only the section 92(4) time limit was, in the Act as passed in 2013.

confirmations.dueText: Within fifteen days of the meeting in which the auditor is appointed.
confirmations.evidence: file a notice of such appointment with the Registrar within fifteen days of the meeting in which the auditor is appointed
confirmations.caveat: Fourth proviso to section 139(1), read in the Act as passed in 2013; later amendments and the form number ADT-1 were not read on an official page.
